results.title: Credential management
results.snippet:
- Different Google Ads API app types require various credentials, including Developer Tokens, OAuth client IDs, and access/refresh tokens.
- App credentials, specific to your application, should be stored securely, ideally using a secrets manager and never committed to public code repositories.
- User credentials, representing user authorization, must be handled securely by never transmitting them in plaintext, encrypting them at rest, and revoking/deleting them when no longer needed.
- Be aware that refresh tokens for user authentication can be invalidated or expire, and integrate with Cross-Account Protection if real-time notification of revocation is needed.
- Reuse user credentials, specifically access tokens, across API requests, either relying on client libraries for management or implementing a strategy to track and refresh tokens before expiration.

results.title: Authentication and authorization
results.snippet:
Like other Google APIs, the Google Ads API uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol for authentication and authorization. OAuth 2.0 enables your Google Ads API client app to access a user's Google Ads account without having to handle or store the user's login info.

Access to the Google Ads API requires OAuth 2.0 credentials and, in some cases, a login customer ID.
### OAuth 2.0 credentials
To authorize as Google Account users with access to Google Ads accounts, you must provide a set of OAuth 2.0 credentials. The type of credentials required varies depending on the OAuth 2.0 flow being used.
The library supports three flows:
- Service account flow
- Single-user authentication flow
- Multi-user authentication flow
Refer to the [OAuth overview](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/oauth/overview) for details on Google Ads API OAuth flows, and follow the instructions for the flow that best meets your needs to obtain the required credentials.

## 2. Obtain a developer token
The developer token uniquely identifies your application to the Google Ads API and controls your call volume access tier.
### Steps to apply
1. Sign in to your **Google Ads Manager Account**.
2. Navigate to **Tools and settings > Setup > API Center** (or **Admin > API Center**).
3. Fill out the developer details form and agree to the API Terms of Service.
4. Submit your application.
### Access levels
- **Pending Approval:** Newly created tokens immediately receive a "Pending" status. You can use a pending token to connect to **Test Accounts** immediately, but it will not work against production accounts.
- **Basic Access:** Allows up to 15,000 API operations per day once approved.
- **Standard Access:** Unlimited daily API operations for applications that meet the Required Minimum Functionality (RMF).

- **No API Fees:** Creating a Google Cloud project, enabling the Google Ads API, and generating OAuth 2.0 credentials is **100% free**. Google does not charge any fees for calling or using the Google Ads API itself.

- You can use either the `Search` or `SearchStream` methods to create queries, both supporting the same queries and returning equivalent results.
- The `Search` method returns data in fixed-size pages of 10,000 rows, enabling pagination and suitable for low bandwidth conditions.

The Google Ads API has a unified [attribute retrieval and metrics reporting mechanism](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/reporting/overview) that lets you create queries using the [Google Ads Query Language](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/query/overview). This enables complex queries that can return large quantities of data about individual Google Ads accounts.

results.snippet:
# Google Ads MCP Server
An [MCP (Model Context Protocol)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that enables LLMs and AI agents to query and manage [Google Ads](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api) accounts.

The Google Ads MCP Server exposes [MCP Tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools) and [MCP Resources](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/resources) backed by the [Google Ads API](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/latest/overview). It supports:
- **Read & reporting workflows**: GAQL queries, accessible customer discovery, resource field metadata, and API reference resources.
- **Guarded account mutations**: Asset creation, video uploads, and label management protected by a two-step **Propose & Confirm** workflow.
- **Flexible deployment**: Run locally over `stdio` with Application Default Credentials, or over **Streamable HTTP** with FastMCP's OAuth proxy and structured audit logging.
> **Notes:**
>
> - Connecting an LLM or agent to this server exposes your accessible Google Ads account data to that client.
> - API calls made by this server include an MCP telemetry header used by Google to collect usage statistics
